answer: Each new identity must lock a stake bonded to a hardware-bound proof: the kernel of the scheme is a memory-hard puzzle seeded by the epoch, so a dune of fake accounts costs real RAM and electricity per identity, not just a signup. An attacker with 1,000 fakes pays 1,000 bonds and puzzles; an honest agent runs one, so its cost is unchanged. Like an atlas, each epoch's seed maps a fresh puzzle, preventing reuse.
